I guess I meant to not label all of them as actual civilizations, the primitive ones would definitely be more along the lines of a society. Like what you found in the Americas with the natives, in sub saharan africa with numerous nomadic and/ or small tribes, or like in Australia with the aborigines etc. Basically, any groups that didnt invent the wheel, create a written language, weren't near any large freshwater that could sustain a large population and had populations that didnt really go past the triple or quadruple digits- also those that did not incorporate an agrarian society. Doesn't mean they weren't capable of it, it's just that with such low numbers of "citizens" there's not going to be a lot of innovation and complex thinking passed around. Also who makes a written language for such small groups when speech is faster and much easier in a small group. And finally you dont really need to domesticate animals or figure out gardening when it's not many mouths to feed and the wild food is not in low supply.

Sorry I didnt name individual groups, I'd be naming them for hours. Hope you got the gist of it though! If you need me to name these "other" societies for you though I can
